In [[mathematics]], the '''pseudospectrum''' of an [[Operator (mathematics)|operator]] is a [[Set (mathematics)|set]] containing the [[spectrum of an operator|spectrum]] of the operator and the numbers that are "almost" [[eigenvalues]]. Knowledge of the pseudospectrum can be particularly useful for understanding [[normal operator|non-normal operator]]s and their eigenfunctions.

The &epsilon;-pseudospectrum of a matrix ''A'' consists of all eigenvalues of matrices which are &epsilon;-close to ''A'':<ref name="Hogben">{{cite book|last1=Hogben|first1=Leslie|authorlink= Leslie Hogben |title=Handbook of Linear Algebra, Second Edition|date=2013|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=9781466507296|page=23-1|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Er7MBQAAQBAJ&dq=pseudospectrum&pg=SA23-PA18|accessdate=8 September 2017|language=en}}</ref>
:<math>\Lambda_\epsilon(A) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} \mid \exists x \in \mathbb{C}^n \setminus \{0\}, \exists E \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n} \colon (A+E)x = \lambda x, \|E\| \leq \epsilon \}.</math>

[[Eigenvalue algorithm|Numerical algorithms which calculate the eigenvalues of a matrix]] give only approximate results due to rounding and other errors. These errors can be described with the matrix ''E''.

More generally, for [[Banach space]]s <math>X,Y </math> and operators <math> A: X \to Y </math> , one can define the <math> \epsilon</math>-pseudospectrum of <math> A </math> (typically denoted by <math> \text{sp}_{\epsilon}(A) </math>) in the following way
:<math>\text{sp}_{\epsilon}(A) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} \mid \|(A-\lambda I)^{-1}\| \geq 1/\epsilon \}.</math>
where we use the convention that <math> \|(A-\lambda I)^{-1}\| = \infty </math> if <math> A - \lambda I </math> is not invertible.<ref name="BottSil">{{cite book|last1=Böttcher|first1=Albrecht|last2=Silbermann|first2=Bernd|author-link1=Albrecht Böttcher|title=Introduction to Large Truncated Toeplitz Matrices|date=1999|publisher=Springer New York|isbn=978-1-4612-1426-7|page=70|doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-1426-7_3|language=en}}</ref>
